svg.font-family: PatrickHandEmbedded, Virgil, 'Segoe Print', 'Comic Sans MS', cursive
svg.title: Native versus managed: two roads from source code to a running program
svg.desc: A hand-drawn comparison with a vertical line marking the moment you run the program. On the native road, almost everything happens before that line: the compiler translates every line, the linker copies library code inside, and the result is one finished file that the CPU runs directly with nothing left to do. On the managed road, the compiler only translates halfway into bytecode and stops; after the line, a runtime loads the libraries, reads the bytecode, and a JIT re-optimises the busy parts while the program runs.
svg.text: Two roads from your code to a running program
The work is the same. The only question is which side of the line it happens on.
Nothing else is decided yet. The rest is
Starts instantly, built for one machine · Slow for a moment then fast, runs anywhere
